title: The LAN port (eno25) negotiated below its speed
status: unreviewed: first estimates by Claude on 2026-11-08, not yet reviewed by the author

causes.title: Cable: damaged, too long, or only two pairs wired
causes.why: gigabit needs all four pairs; a cable with two working pairs falls back to 100 Mb/s with no error.

causes.title: The switch/router port only does 100 Mb/s
causes.why: cheap or ISP-supplied equipment often has Fast Ethernet ports.

causes.title: The other end has its speed forced
causes.why: a forced partner makes autonegotiation fall back, usually to half duplex.

causes.title: This NIC port or its PHY is faulty
causes.why: rare; swapping to another I350 port tells.

evidence.title: Full duplex was negotiated
evidence.why: a forced partner usually ends in a duplex mismatch (half duplex here).

evidence.title: Auto-negotiation is on here
evidence.why: both ends negotiated, which fits a cable or a slower partner.
